sections.overview: This widespread pierid butterfly ranges from southeastern Europe across temperate Asia to Japan and Taiwan.
sections.identification: It is yellow with dark markings near the forewing tip.
sections.habitat: It frequents dry grasslands, steppes and alfalfa fields, including foothills and mountain slopes.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on legumes such as alfalfa and crown vetch.
sections.behavior: It is an inland migrant with a tendency to expand its range; several generations may fly in a year.
sections.reproduction: In Japan, the caterpillar overwinters on host plants and may continue feeding during mild winter weather.
sections.ecology: Its alfalfa use overlaps with that of Colias croceus, but the two remain distinct species with useful wing-pattern differences.
sections.conservation: A Mediterranean regional assessment lists it as Least Concern; that category is regional, not a global assessment.
